Find the area (in square units) of $△ABC$ shown above.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC.
$$

We are given that $m∠A={60}^{∘}.$ Notice that relative to $∠A,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{BC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{AB}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠A) & =\frac{BC}{AB} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡({60}^{∘}) & =\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{3}\,x} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{x+2}{\sqrt{3}\,x} \\ \sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}\,x) & =x+2 \\ 3x & =x+2 \\ 2x & =2 \\ x & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are 

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =x+2=1+2=3, \\ AB & =\sqrt{3}\,x=\sqrt{3}(1)=\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot AB\cdot BC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot 3 \\  & =\frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
